searchText: I have a few questions: * How many storage slots does a typical transaction touch? * How many logs do transactions use, on average? How many bytes do the logs use? * How much memory do transactions actually expand? also would be helpful to know the 95th and 99th percentiles (any range in the past ~5m blocks is probably fine) Has anyone done any analysis like this? We looked at maximum memory, but can't remember the details, cc <@!425343240212971521> <@!425274498732916736>. Yeah I was thinking I had seen a post about that from you guys at one point, but couldn't find it in my history! And here's the final update (at least from our side) on the topic of code merkleization/chunking by <@!425343240212971521> and <@!259648573401071617>: https://notes.ethereum.org/@ipsilon/code-merkleization-implementation-analysis > TLDR: In this work we implemented Code Merkleization in go-ethereum, including code proof generation (using FastSSZ). We have analyzed the performance (in terms of proof size) of different proof implementations on ~1M mainnet blocks. Lastly we provide direction for further work using Verkle Trees. I was wondering why the function signature in the EVM ABI is represented by just 4 bytes rather than a full 32 byte keccak hash (as is the case with log events). Was it just to save on memory/state usage? Seems like this at least partly contributed to yesterday's $600M hack. A good question for the Solidity devs, as that is their thing not an EVM thing. Ah— sorry about that! I'd be very interested in stats on memory usage.

* How much memory do transactions actually expand?

And here's the final update (at least from our side) on the topic of code merkleization/chunking by <@!425343240212971521> and <@!259648573401071617>: https://notes.ethereum.org/@ipsilon/code-merkleization-implementation-analysis

> TLDR: In this work we implemented Code Merkleization in go-ethereum, including code proof generation (using FastSSZ).
